rows.behavior: The OpenCode agent translator keeps description, adds mode: subagent, writes permission with "*": deny first and then allow for each mapped tool (Read to read, Grep to grep, Glob to glob, Write and Edit to edit, Bash to shell), drops name, color, effort and model, copies the body unchanged, gives the same bytes for the same input, and refuses, naming the tool, a Claude tool not in its map.
rows.fails_when: any mapping differs, "*": deny is not the first rule, a tools key or a Claude-only key survives, the body changes, two runs differ, or an unknown tool translates silently

rows.behavior: In a repository whose lock shows kmctl's package installed for OpenCode, kmctl plugin patch rewrites .opencode/agents/kmctl-auditor.md, bundle-weaver.md and event-analyzer.md into the translated form (the auditor allows only read, grep and glob), writes kmctl's four rules to .opencode/rules/ without their applyTo front matter, merges ".opencode/rules/*.md" into opencode.json's instructions once while keeping every other key (mcp included), writes .opencode/plugins/kmctl.js, and writes nothing under .agents/plugins/; a second patch changes no file.
rows.fails_when: a file is missing, extra or differs from that description, another opencode.json key changes or is lost, the instructions entry appears twice, anything is written under .agents/plugins/, or a second patch changes a file

rows.behavior: kmctl plugin patch refuses, naming the file, an opencode.json that is not valid JSON, and leaves it unchanged.
rows.fails_when: patch exits 0, names no file, or changes the file

rows.behavior: Harnesses are told apart correctly now that .agents/skills/ is shared: a lock with only OpenCode files (.opencode/ plus .agents/skills/) reads as opencode only, one with Antigravity's rules or hooks reads as antigravity, and both read as both, in plugin.py and in doctor.
rows.fails_when: an OpenCode-only lock reads as antigravity, or any of the three cases gives the wrong harnesses in either module
rows.command: uv run pytest tests/test_opencode.py tests/test_plugin_patch.py tests/test_doctor.py -k harnesses -q

rows.behavior: The briefing plugin .opencode/plugins/kmctl.js, loaded under node with a stub ctx, registers one context hook that pushes the kmctl briefing as a {type: "text"} system part, and when kmctl is not on PATH or kmctl briefing fails it registers nothing or pushes nothing, and neither setup nor the hook throws or rejects (I1).
rows.fails_when: the text pushed differs from kmctl briefing's output, or with kmctl missing or failing setup or the hook throws, rejects, or pushes a part; the test skips only when node is not on PATH

rows.behavior: kmctl plugin patch --undo deletes the three translated agents, the four rules, the instructions entry (and opencode.json when patch created it and nothing else is left) and the plugin file, and nothing else; patch --scope user leaves OpenCode alone and says so.
rows.fails_when: a kmctl file is left, a file kmctl did not write is removed or changed, or --scope user writes under .opencode/ or says nothing
rows.command: uv run pytest tests/test_opencode.py -k "undo or user_scope" -q

rows.behavior: kmctl doctor, for an OpenCode install, runs opencode.lock, opencode.files, opencode.okf-skills, opencode.agents, opencode.rules, opencode.okf-mcp, opencode.hook and dep.opencode; after a bare apm install (agents back in Claude format), a hand-edited rule, a missing instructions entry, a missing okf-bundle entry or an edited plugin, the matching check fails with a fix naming kmctl plugin patch or apm install --target opencode; on a freshly patched install every check but dep.opencode (when opencode is not on PATH) passes; doctor's help lists the new checks.
rows.fails_when: any listed fault goes unreported, a fix names neither command, a clean install fails a check, or the help omits a check
rows.command: uv run pytest tests/test_opencode.py tests/test_doctor.py -k opencode -q

rows.behavior: In a scratch consumer, apm install --target opencode (APM 0.33.0) of kmctl's package served from a local git server, then kmctl plugin patch, leaves kmctl's and okf's skills in .agents/skills/, the four rules, the three translated agents, the plugin, and opencode.json with the instructions entry and okf-bundle as {type: local, enabled: true, command: [sh, -c, ...]}; a second apm install then kmctl plugin patch changes no file; patch --undo then apm uninstall exits 0 and leaves no kmctl or okf file.
rows.fails_when: any step fails, any of those is missing or differs, a reinstall plus patch changes a file, or the uninstall fails or leaves files
rows.command: uv run pytest tests/test_opencode.py -m integration -k consumer -q

rows.behavior: With opencode on PATH, OpenCode loads the three translated agents (opencode agent list, or its equivalent, names kmctl-auditor, bundle-weaver and event-analyzer as subagents); the test skips when opencode is absent.
rows.fails_when: opencode is present and any of the three agents is missing from its list
rows.command: uv run pytest tests/test_opencode.py -m integration -k loads_agents -q

rows.behavior: A new decision records the OpenCode route (APM for skills and okf's server, patch for agents, rules through instructions, and the V2 briefing plugin), the tool map, that every rule loads every session, that apm install reverts the agents so patch runs after every install and --undo runs before apm uninstall, why apm audit reports drift, and a table of the gaps with when to drop each; the manifesto names OpenCode and no longer lists it as out of scope; docs/reference/commands.md documents what patch, --undo and doctor do for OpenCode; the install how-to and README give the OpenCode install, that every rule always loads, and that okf's server needs uv.
rows.fails_when: any of those is missing, or the decision does not match kmctl schema decision
uv run pytest or uv run pytest -m integration fails
rows.command: uv run pytest -q -m "not integration or integration"
